newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle end mixed ahead of USDA report.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle end mixed ahead of USDA report.

text.p: CME live cattle futures ended mixed ahead of the monthly USDA Cattle on Feed report after showing gains early. Feeder cattle held gains into the close, bolstered by lower corn futures, traders said.

Live cattle closed 0.650 cent per lb higher to 0.050 lower with August up most and October up 0.375 at 70.200 cents. Feeder cattle ended up 0.075 to 0.600 cent a lb with October up the least at 80.925 cents.
Short covering lifted live cattle into buy stops early, but prices drifted back and turned mixed on position-evening ahead of the report, they said.

Support was attributed to expectations of higher boxed beef prices next week and indications feedlots will ask higher prices. Feedlots were seen selling cattle at $66 per cwt next week. Deliveries were also going to strong hands and spreads bought cattle and sold hogs, sources noted.

On-feed estimates for USDA's monthly Cattle on Feed report averaged 115.6 percent of a year ago and ranged from 114 to 117.8 percent in the major seven cattle-feeding states. July placement estimates averaged 100.8 percent and ranged from 96 to 106.5 percent while July marketings estimates averaged 105.5 percent, in a range from 103 to 107 percent.

LFG notably bought August early while Cargill Investor Services and RBH bought October. R.J. O'Brien was on both sides. In options, one commercial actively bought December 70 puts while other commercials were hedging, buying puts and selling calls in December and February, pit sources said.
Lower corn futures again supported feeder cattle but trade was slow at times ahead of the report, traders said.
The latest CME feeder cattle index was off $0.29 at $80.90 per cwt.
Refco and ADM Investor Services bought October feeders early while Smith Barney and Lind-Waldock sold, pit sources said.

Boneless beef futures rose after posting losses much of the week with buying by locals from live cattle providing much of the early advance. But late liquidation weighed on August. Expectations beef prices will firm next week provided the bulk of suppot, traders said.

Boneless beef futures closed 0.40 cent per lb lower to 0.70 higher with October up most at 94.00 cents. Trimmings ended mixed at 0.70 cent a lb lower to 0.20 higher with only August off and October up most at 44.70 cents.
